title: On Pascual Jordan's Erweiterte Gravitationstheorie
speaker: Bernadette Lessel (University of Bonn)
description: UPAC Colloquium (Utrecht Philosophy of Astronomy & Cosmology): research presentation, no preparation needed. Hybrid; the Teams link goes out via the upac-l mailing list. To join the speaker for dinner, e-mail cosmo-master.assistant@uu.nl the day before.
abstract: Pascual Jordan is mostly known as one of the founding figures of quantum mechanics. In the late 1930s, however, he became interested in cosmological questions, driven by a fascination with large dimensionless natural constants. This line of inquiry developed into a relativistic theory of gravitation involving a variable gravitational constant, formulated within the mathematical framework of projective relativity. In this talk, I trace Jordan's path from his 1937 paper on large dimensionless numbers to the post-war formulation of his extended theory, and explain its main features.
